CheckTitle: Ensure DMARC records are published for all Exchange Online domains
Description: **Microsoft 365 Exchange Online domains** should have **DMARC TXT records** published in DNS with an enforcing policy. This evaluates each accepted domain to confirm a DMARC record exists at _dmarc.<domain> with p=quarantine or p=reject to prevent domain spoofing and phishing attacks.
Risk:
Without **DMARC** (or with p=none), attackers can **impersonate your domain** to send spoofed or phishing emails that appear to come from your organization.

This enables **business email compromise (BEC)**, credential theft, malware delivery, and reputational damage. DMARC builds on SPF and DKIM to provide enforcement and reporting.

Code.Other:
1. Sign in to Microsoft 365 Defender: https://security.microsoft.com
2. Go to Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Email authentication settings > DMIM
3. Review the DMARC status for each domain
4. Publish a DMARC TXT record at _dmarc.<domain> with v=DMARC1; p=quarantine (or p=reject) at your DNS provider
5. After DMARC is in place, monitor reports and move from p=none to p=quarantine to p=reject

Recommendation.Text:
- Publish **DMARC records** for all sending domains and subdomains
- Start with **p=none** to monitor, then progress to **p=quarantine** and finally **p=reject**
- Combine with **SPF** and **DKIM** for defense in depth
- Review DMARC aggregate and forensic reports regularly to detect spoofing attempts
